outcome: No proof, disproof, or new record for the maximum number of givens in a minimal Sudoku puzzle has appeared since 26 January 2024; the empirical record of 40 clues (found by forum user 'dobrichev', reported around 2010–2014, predating the window) remains the largest known minimal puzzle and is still unproven as an actual maximum.
summary: This bullet asks for the maximum number of givens (clues) a *minimal* Sudoku puzzle (one where removing any clue destroys uniqueness) can have. This is the mirror image of the famous 17-clue minimum problem, which was settled in 2012 (McGuire, Tugemann, Civario), but the maximum-givens question has no comparable exhaustive-search proof: it is a much larger, less constrained search space (the current record, 40 clues, was found by exhaustive/targeted computer search by the forum contributor known as 'dobrichev', with the relevant forum threads and Wikipedia record dating to roughly 2010-2014, well before the 26 January 2024 frozen revision). I searched broadly for any post-window movement: a new record above 40 clues, a proof that 40 (or some other number) is the true maximum, or any theoretical upper bound result. I found none. I also checked a 2023/2024 paper ('How Many Clues To Give? A Bilevel Formulation for the Minimum Sudoku Clue Problem', arXiv:2305.01697, journal version dated 7 March 2024 on ScienceDirect) which is superficially adjacent but addresses a different question — the minimum number of clues needed to pin down a *given* completed grid (MSCP), not the maximum number of givens compatible with minimality — so it is out of scope under §3.1 (a related/different problem, not a case of this one), and in any case its arXiv preprint predates the window. I also searched for any AI/LLM involvement specific to this combinatorial question; the only AI-and-Sudoku material I found (Sudoku-Bench, causal-language-modeling-on-logic-puzzles papers, Sakana AI's Sudoku work) concerns LLMs solving/reasoning about Sudoku puzzles generally (and performing poorly, e.g. sub-15% solve rates reported for o3-mini-high and Gemini 2.5 Pro on Sudoku variants), and has no connection to the maximum-givens-for-a-minimal-puzzle question. The Wikipedia 'Mathematics of Sudoku' article, as of this check, still states only that '40 clues' is the largest minimal puzzle found so far, with no update. Given the topic is a niche combinatorial/computational puzzle question mostly discussed on the enjoysudoku forum and personal collection pages, and I found nothing there or in the academic literature suggesting new activity, I classify this as open with no_change_found true, matching the triage's 'none' verdict.
competing_reading: None found — I found no borderline case or ambiguous result to weigh a different classification against. It is conceivable that a new record puzzle (e.g. 41+ clues) has been posted only on the enjoysudoku forum without being indexed by general web search or picked up by Wikipedia, since that forum is the primary venue for this niche pursuit and is not always well-crawled; I could not directly browse the current state of relevant forum threads (a direct fetch of one thread failed with a connection error) so I cannot fully rule this out.
what_would_settle_it: A post-26-January-2024 announcement (forum post, paper, or updated Wikipedia/Mathematics-of-Sudoku text) reporting either (a) a minimal Sudoku puzzle with more than 40 givens, or (b) a proof/exhaustive argument that 40 is the true maximum for minimal puzzles.
